A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Playmate framework. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original video-generation benchmarks, CFG and adaptive-normalization ablations, and a Gaussian-noise augmentation experiment in Appendix A.2.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds emotion-control comparisons, a user study, pose-accuracy measurements and disentanglement examples.

M1.justification: The latent representation, motion-decoupled module, diffusion transformer, two-stage emotion controller, CFG procedure and appendix noise augmentation are unchanged. The new disentanglement demonstrations test existing capabilities rather than introduce a method component.

E1.justification: The represented datasets and portrait-animation, emotion-control and pose-control tasks remain unchanged. MEAD already supplied emotion-training data in v2; its new test comparison and the additional ratings and control analyses extend evaluation within existing coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 2 newly evaluates EAMM, DreamTalk, EDTalk and EAT against Playmate, substantially expanding comparison methods for the central emotion-control contribution. The five existing video-generation baselines remain unchanged and also participate in the new user study.

E3.justification: v3 adds a MEAD emotion-comparison protocol, a 10-participant study using 1–5 ratings for four perceptual metrics, APD measurements in Appendix A.3, and fixed-latent controls in A.4. Existing training and preprocessing settings remain unchanged; Emo-A was already used in v2's CFG ablation.

E4.justification: Appendix A.4 and Figure 10 add a targeted disentanglement analysis: generated poses with fixed facial dynamics, and generated facial dynamics with fixed or predefined spinning poses. The adaptive-normalization, CFG and Gaussian-noise ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new user study reports mean ratings and participant count without variability or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial results: emotion accuracy of 0.550 versus EDTalk's 0.460 in Table 2; user-study rankings favoring Playmate for video definition and visual appeal, but Sonic for lip sync and naturalness; and pose APD results and disentanglement examples. Table 1 and the CFG results, renumbered from Table 2 to Table 4, are numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(10), covering latent transformations, losses, normalization, diffusion guidance and noise augmentation, are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, mathematical derivations or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion narrow the claim of outperforming state-of-the-art methods in lip synchronization to competitive or strong performance. The central framework, video-quality and controllability claims remain intact.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 explicitly acknowledges Sonic's better lip-sync scores and discusses Playmate's greater control flexibility alongside higher implementation complexity. The existing limitations concerning facial scope, extreme head movements, rendering artifacts and backgrounds remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The promised code-access location changes from the project homepage to a specific GitHub repository. Both versions still describe future availability, so this does not establish a release. Hardware, training times, preprocessing and disclosed hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds the EDTalk reference and expands positioning against Sonic by discussing controllability and complexity. The remaining cited works and the related-work organization are retained; the Tan 2024 citation suffix changes reflect the added reference.

P1.justification: Changes include localized wording and typo corrections, revised abstract and conclusion passages, expanded results discussion, and new appendix subsections A.3–A.4. Most prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Three new tables present emotion comparisons, user ratings and pose accuracy, while the new multirow Figure 10 displays disentanglement controls. This substantially expands the visual evidence. All nine earlier figures are retained; some material moves, and the renumbered CFG table gains best/second-best highlighting.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens evidence for the central controllability contribution: v2 offered emotion demonstrations and CFG sweeps, whereas v3 adds comparisons against four emotion-control methods, quantitative pose evaluation and direct disentanglement checks. The user study provides complementary perceptual evidence, and the narrowed lip-sync claims better match Table 1. Sparse new protocol details and absent uncertainty reporting limit confidence, but the added validation and better-calibrated claims constitute a substantial overall improvement.
